title: A fully-made Tahia
creator: Prakriti Panda
source_statement: Own work, identified by the photographer’s file title as a fully-made tahia. Source page identifies India; it does not name the pictured person, maker or workshop.
licence_basis: Direct Commons source wikitext contains {{self|cc-by-sa-4.0}} and own-work declaration; original API metadata independently repeats author/licence. Reuse rests on this specific Commons licence, not a general licence inferred for PARI photographs.
visual_review: Complete curved white floral headpiece above a worn worktable, held by a hand; other hand and cropped torso visible, face absent. Petal layers, small rounded buds, green supports and cut scraps are legible; the headpiece remains completely inside the source frame. Background is softly focused. Strong authentic documentary photograph suitable for the making-focused essay.
inspection_method: Original download verified against Commons SHA1 and dimensions. Native large-image display exceeded tool output size, so the original was visually inspected through a temporary1500px full-frame PNG in /tmp. That inspection-only copy is not a delivered asset; both saved JPEGs remain byte-identical originals.
alt: A hand holds a curved white floral headpiece above a worktable.
caption: A finished tahia, photographed in 2022.
credit: Prakriti Panda, “A fully-made Tahia”, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0. Unmodified.
identity_limits: The Commons file does not identify the pictured person, exact workshop, maker or locality. Do not attribute the visible hand to Upendra Kumar Purohit from photographer/date similarity alone.
Do not identify this as Jagannath’s ceremonial tahia or infer that different tahia traditions are interchangeable.
Photograph does not establish plant species or the composition of every visible component; material/process statements require the article’s independent evidence.
Treat the photograph and PARI report as one conservative source family for derivative-word allocation.
